act_title: A Nocturne of the Far North

quests.title: In the Shifting Light of the Moon

dialogue.t: Thank you for waiting. I've finished checking your Adventurer Handbook. Here are your commission rewards.
We have no other urgent commissions on the books at present. Thank you for all your hard work lately. Perhaps you two could consider taking a vacation.
Amazing! Paimon never thought we'd end up having down time in Nod-Krai.
Things were pretty hectic when we first got here. Everywhere you looked, it was either The Wild Hunt causing chaos or the Fatui stirring up trouble...
It felt like this whole region was one giant slime-in-a-barrel, ready to go "boom" at any moment!

dialogue.sit: We really have achieved a lot since we've been here, haven't we?
The Traveler and Paimon strike again.

dialogue.t: Sure have... Things were looking pretty dicey, but in the end we managed to turn it around. ...Whoa, Paimon just got deja vu... Oh, that's right — it's because we've done this, like, a million times now, hehe.
Ah, yes. Are you two aware that the Moon-Prayer Night is soon to take place?
Oh yeah! Lauma told us that was coming up soon.
Wait, why do you mention it, though? Do people in Nasha Town celebrate it too? Paimon thought it was just for Moon Goddess worshipers.
You're partially right. Most people in Nasha Town just see the festival as an opportunity to do business. They do not concern themselves with the religious element.
The festival was first celebrated by the Frostmoon Scions. On this day, they would wear Moon-Prayer Blossoms and celebrate the birth of the Moon Goddess through song and dance.
They would also prepare food and handicrafts, and give them as gifts to others. Over time, it became Nod-Krai's most lively festival.
Ooh, sounds like fun!

dialogue.sit: I'm definitely up for it.

dialogue.t: Great! Hehe, well, in the meantime, since Katheryne doesn't have any commissions for us, let's focus on some personal business instead.
When we first got here, you mentioned that this was where your spaceship landed.
We didn't get to follow up on it at the time, 'cause we got wrapped up in that whole Rerir situation. But now, we can finally start investigating it properly!

dialogue.sit: Except, we have no idea where to start...

dialogue.t: Well... There's a saying Paimon's heard around these parts, which goes: "If you lift up a rock, you'll find something you weren't looking for."
By that logic, you'll never find what you're looking for while you're searching, but the moment you stop looking, it'll jump right out at you!

dialogue.sit: I'm not sure it's as simple as that...

dialogue.t: Could be worth a try though, right? Anyway, Paimon suggests we focus on other stuff we wanna do for now, and just keep an ear out for spaceship-related intel as we go.

dialogue.sit: (We haven't seen Columbina in a while...)
(She used a huge amount of power in the final battle against Rerir, and has been much weaker since then.)
(I don't know if I can do anything to genuinely help her... but surely a little chat can do no harm.)
(One other thing that concerns me is... We've seen no trace of The Doctor so far.)

dialogue.t: What's wrong? You look super serious all of a sudden.

dialogue.sit: I was just thinking about Columbina and The Doctor.

dialogue.t: Huh!? Paimon gets why you'd be concerned about Columbina... But what does The Doctor have to do with anything?

dialogue.sit: We learned back in Natlan that he's been investigating the moon...
But he's been suspiciously absent so far.

dialogue.t: Oh, that's true... And now that you mention it, we're definitely overdue for a showdown with the Fatui!
It is weird that he hasn't shown himself this whole time... What could he be up to?

dialogue.sit: Engrossed in one of his experiments, perhaps.
Either way, his current inaction is a good thing.

dialogue.t: True. Paimon would much rather deal with Marionette, anyway. She says the meanest things, but when it comes down to it, she doesn't seem like a bad person.
Maybe it's the pressure of being a Fatuus? Especially as a harbinger. Does she feel like she's gotta act tough to keep up appearances or something?

dialogue.sit: Um... M—Maybe?

dialogue.t: But then, every time we had it out with Rerir, she always wound up having to repair Pulonia and her other robots.
That's gotta sting... Losing face always hurts more for people who care a lot about their image. She's probably still furious about it...

dialogue.sit: Uh, Paimon...
I have a feeling she might've heard that.

dialogue.t: What? Relax, she's not even here— Huh!?
...What's the matter?
Oh, nothing, nothing. Sorry, we'll be on our way now...
Where were we, again? Oh yeah, Columbina? Right, yeah, let's go see Columbina, hehehe...
Hey, she's sitting up!
Is me sitting here a rare sight?

dialogue.sit: No. We just thought you'd be resting.

dialogue.t: Perhaps I would have been, were it not for the sudden arrival of some unexpected guests.
Not that I consider it a disturbance. After all, you are the only ones who are free to enter.
...Would it not be a little unfriendly of me to lie down while we speak?

dialogue.sit: I didn't realize you put so much thought into little things like that.

dialogue.t: Only sometimes. There have been moments lately where I think about you and your companions.
They are warm, mysterious, and cozy memories. Very few of my past memories are anything like that.
...They say that travelers return home bearing bags full of souvenirs. But my luggage was empty, and I believed it would stay that way.
Return home...? So, you're still planning on returning to the moon...
Yes. This planet continues to reject me, reminding me that I do not belong here.
If I remain in Teyvat, there will come a day that I disintegrate. And I don't mean reduced to dust, or turned into food for the flowers. I mean, I will cease to exist entirely.
Alright then. Well, we're sure gonna miss you... but it sounds like we'll have to say goodbye.

dialogue.sit: How do you intend to return?

dialogue.t: The Moon-Prayer Night is soon to arrive. On that day, the moon will be closest to Teyvat.
The kuuvahki in this land will reach its peak at that time. I merely need to grasp the tide, and with relatively little effort...
Ooh, Paimon gets it. It'll work like a slingshot!

dialogue.sit: You make it sound like she's gonna get blasted up to the moon.

dialogue.t: If I did that, I suspect I would crash into the false sky.
I will be using a much gentler approach. But I do like the analogy. It's fun.
Hehe, you see? She gets Paimon's sense of humor.

dialogue.sit: In the blink of an eye, the time has come to part ways.

dialogue.t: It does feel that way, doesn't it? Time seems to fly fastest when you are enjoying it.
I have always thought of myself as a wanderer on this earth. And it has never expressed any desire to keep me here.
Yet just as I plan to depart, it tugs at my arm... Is this a gesture of affection, or is the world mocking me?

dialogue.sit: Oh... Were you hoping I can answer that?

dialogue.t: Yes. You are a Traveler, so you must have a lot of experience in this area.

dialogue.sit: Then, what I would say is... enjoy the moment.

dialogue.t: That's right! Don't overthink it. Happiness is happiness, and joy is joy. The point is to enjoy it, not analyze it.
I see. Then, what I would say is... even though I am very tired right now, I am still happy.

dialogue.sit: I can't tell from the tone of your voice.

dialogue.t: Oh, really? You... don't think I sound happy?

dialogue.sit: I'm just kidding. I could tell you were in a good mood today from the moment we saw you.

dialogue.t: Ah. A joke. Albeit not a funny one.
Anyway. I assume you're here about you-know-what? Give me your hand.

dialogue.sit: Actually, it's not that. There's something else we wanted to discuss with you.

dialogue.t: Oh. Then, do you still want to give me your hand, or not?

dialogue.sit: ...Sure.
Thank you. So, I've heard that in the Moon-Prayer Nights of the past, people here would hold celebrations in the Moon Goddess's honor.
Since you helped so much in our fight against the Rächer of Solnari, I think you deserve a farewell party before you return home.
I haven't asked everyone else for their opinions on this yet, but I'd like to invite you to join the upcoming Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogue.t: ...I've never joined a Moon-Prayer Night before. I'm not sure what I would even do.
Oh, don't worry about that. We'd take care of everything! All you'd need to do is show up.
Of course, there's no need to force it if you're not feeling strong enough. It's just, this kinda felt like a golden opportunity...
But, they call me Kuutar. And the Fatui have an arrest warrant out for me. I shouldn't appear in public right now...

dialogue.sit: (Yeah, there will definitely be complications... but...)
I'll make it work. You have my word.

dialogue.t: Yeah, we got your back! Well, he(she) does. Paimon's actually not too sure what he's(she's) planning...
Alright. If you're sure... I will not refuse your invitation.
I suppose it wouldn't hurt to pack a few more sights from this world into my suitcase before finally learning what my homeland looks like.
Oh, if you see Lauma, please tell her that my answer to the question she asked me is neither "yes" nor "no."
Rather, it is "there is no need."
Uhh... That was kinda cryptic, but sure. Guess it's between the two of you. We'll pass along the message. Bye for now!
And also... I do not know...
Y—You won't snitch on us, will you?
I'm not entirely sure what you're talking about. But rest assured, I protect client and adventurer confidentiality as a matter of principle.
Phew, that's a relief... Paimon does not wanna get an earful from her...
Hey Lauma, it's us! ...Huh? Varka? What are you doing here?
Hahaha, beats me. I had a bit too much to drink last night, and when I woke up, I was on Hiisi Island.
Mr. Varka is helping to oversee Nasha Town's preparations for Moon-Prayer Night. He is here to go over some details regarding the decorations and custom cloth designs.
Right, yeah. That too.
What do you mean, "that too"!?

dialogue.sit: So, preparations are already underway?

dialogue.t: Yes. Celebrating this festival is a long-held tradition here in Nod-Krai.
On this day, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance. Our people take these to be blessed omens.
It's an especially welcome event coming off the back of all that nasty business with Rerir. Everyone got put through the wringer recently, and now they're looking to turn their fortunes around.
The big shots in town all agree that a big, lively celebration is just what we need to rebuild people's faith in this place.
No wonder Katheryne said that people weren't so bothered about the religious element.
That's right, it's become more of a local custom by this point. The celebrations have little to do with whether the religious stories behind this event are true or not.
Even the Frostmoon Scions are eagerly awaiting the coming of Moon-Prayer Night, despite now knowing that their past beliefs were founded on a falsehood.
That's fair. It's a bit like the Lantern Rite in Liyue. It's a chance for people to enjoy themselves, not debate the existence of the adepti.

dialogue.sit: Although, in their case, the adepti definitely do exist...
We've met plenty of them in our time...

dialogue.t: Oh, one other thing — we just went to see Columbina. We went ahead and invited her to take part in the festival this time. Hope that's okay.
Wait, so... You mean, she agreed to it? Huh. That's quite a surprise.
Then I suppose that she intends to return to the moon on that day.
Oh, yeah. It's kind of a complicated process, but basically... Uh... It's like a slingshot!

dialogue.sit: She probably shouldn't have endorsed your metaphor...

dialogue.t: I understand. Hm... In truth, I had a feeling that she might make such a decision.
Well, if Kuutar has decided to participate in the festival, we should prepare accordingly.
Yeah, exactly! She was saying how it could be risky for her to show her face in public. We were wondering if there was any way we could hide her...
Hmm... Unfortunately, the people who carved the statues did an excellent job of capturing her likeness. It will be very challenging to hide a goddess whose face everyone is so familiar with...
Darn. We may have bitten off more than we can chew here...
Ah, don't sweat the small stuff! We can handle that.
Huh? Are you saying you have a plan?
Not as such, no. But the most important thing with a festival is to keep the mood light and your spirits up.
You can't go preparing for a festival with those long faces. You'll never convince anyone to enjoy themselves!
The Mondstadter spirit is strong with this one...
As it happens, I agree with Mr. Varka.
Let's start by making our appreciation for Kuutar the beating heart of the festive atmosphere.
And who knows? Once we get the ball rolling, perhaps everything will just... fall into place?
Hey! Did you catch that? Lauma said the thing! Or, close enough at least!
Hmm...?

Haha, I'm looking forward to the Moon-Prayer Night already... We have a festival in Mondstadt called Windblume, and you could always tell which couples are celebrating it for their first time by the smiles on their faces. Big, beaming smiles, like their whole face is glowing.
And I have a feeling we'll get to see that same smile on the Moon Goddess's face at this festival.
Uhh... Not quite the same, surely...
Anyway, I'll take care of business in the city, but I'll have to leave the decor up to you and the Frostmoon Scions. No one else can capture that traditional aesthetic quite like you guys.
But lastly, there's the final key element that brings the festival to life — companionship.

dialogue.sit: We'll take care of that part.

dialogue.t: Before you leave, let me show you something that we've been preparing. Mr. Varka had asked to see it already, so you may as well tag along.
...Also, I have some further questions about Kuutar's decision.
Moon-Prayer Night's nearly here! Hehe, candy, here we come!
Don't go feeding all the candy to the animals...
I—I wasn't gonna!
We're fully focused on festival preparations at the moment. So far, it's all going well.
Please have patience. The Moon-Prayer Night will soon be upon us.
This Moonveil doesn't seem translucent enough...
I think I should take it down and work on it some more.
The frame is done, and I've got a nice new set of tools. Yep, this is looking good.
Huh. What's this? They sure look like they're having fun.
I believe so. Kuuhenki seem very skilled at playing drums like these, although I'm not sure where they learned it from...
Maybe it's an innate talent? In their eyes, they're probably just playing with toys.
Luonnotar! You wanna play too?

dialogue.sit: Guess not...

dialogue.t: Yeah... She looks more confused than anything.
Maybe we can teach her next time if we get the chance.
Everyone seems hard at work...
They are preparing items for Moon-Prayer Night. For instance, the sculpture being made over here. Mr. Varka and I were just finalizing the details of where it will be placed.
Ah, there she is. I didn't know the finished article would be so large...
Not to worry, though, all the necessary arrangements have been made. Just let me know once it's ready, and I'll get some people to ship it over.
You have my thanks. And over here, we are preparing a very traditional confection.
Aw, look at all these colors. It looks great! Can Paimon try one?
Hehe, of course. I have a feeling you'll like it a lot.
You bet! Sweets and treats are Paimon's favorite!
Haha, if you included those in the Feast of the Moon, I bet Paimon would have joined the Frostmoon Scions by now.
There will also be Verdant Crests like this present in Nasha Town during the festival.
The timing of Moon-Prayer Night is not completely set in advance. We make a rough estimate, then observe the changes in the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms to guide us.
As such, the wait itself is a fun feature of this particular festival.
Let's talk here. To tell the truth, I am very surprised to hear that Kuutar is willing to participate in the festival.
I once asked her if she'd be willing to stay with the Frostmoon Scions. I could introduce her to everyone, and we could be a family to one another.
She did not answer, but she has not appeared here since.
I took this to mean her answer was "no," but if that were the case, she would not have accepted this invitation...

dialogue.sit: Speaking of answers, she asked us to pass along a message:
There is no need.

dialogue.t: Ah...
I see... Maybe she is right. Maybe the Frostmoon Scions of today no longer need a Moon Goddess.
But my wish was not for her to come here and be worshiped as a deity. I simply wanted to offer her a place to stay.
I'm sure she believes that showing herself here might invite Fatui intervention, and as such, she does not wish to cause us trouble.
But what really pains me about all this is that... This is her birthplace, she ought to belong here, yet no one has been able to grant her shelter.

I think I'm qualified to weigh in here... When someone's about to depart on a long trip, what they need is blessings, not burdens. We should wish her the best, not make the journey harder than it already is.
Anyway, she's agreed to attend, hasn't she? All we need to do is simply respect her decision.
I see your point... Yes, she will soon depart, after all.
Our job is to leave her with some happy memories. Besides, who's to say her journey to the moon is a one-way trip? It's not like she can't come back and visit if she wants, right?
Paimon agrees wholeheartedly! Festivals are all about having fun, so let's keep it simple!
Alright, I'm gonna head back to Nasha Town soon. Wanna come with? I'm guessing you have some other folks to visit there.
Sure thing, let's go. Bye for now, Lauma!
Thank you all. Goodbye.

dialogue.sit: (A traveler needs blessings, not burdens...)
(It sounds good in principle. But will blessings alone be enough for Columbina?)

dialogue.t: Hmm? Hey, over there... It's Durin and Albedo with Flins. What could they be chatting about?
Your guess is as good as mine.
Ah, Grand Master. And {NICKNAME} and Paimon.
Hello there. It's been a while.
Perfect, we have some new volunteers for our investigation.

dialogue.sit: Sorry, what investigation?

dialogue.t: Wait, wait, let me guess... The righteous Lightkeepers are finally ready to hunt down the Abyssal dragon?
Haha. Yes, that too.
Yeah, right! Uh... Wait, why does everyone keep saying "that too"?
Well, to be precise, the facts match, but not the causality.
Wait, so I guessed right!?
Half right! Don't act so impressed with yourself!
Um, maybe I can explain... We ran into Mr. Flins north of Nasha Town.
At that time, we'd just noticed a few Abyssal creatures out in the wild, but the strange thing was... I didn't detect any traces of Abyssal energy on them at all.
On closer inspection, we realized that they were not real monsters, but something akin to reflections in the water... or perhaps a mirage.
Huh? What do you mean? Like, you could see them but not touch them?
Exactly. It was very peculiar. They roared and tried to attack us, but we could not make any physical contact with them.
I think I've heard of things like that happening in Nod-Krai before... but I don't know much about it.
Yes, it's a known phenomenon. Mirage-like illusions tend to appear in Nod-Krai in the run-up to Moon-Prayer Night.
From a distance, they appear quite real.
I myself thought that Misters Durin and Albedo were locked in battle with Abyssal monsters when I first arrived.
But after sharing intel and investigating a little further, we can confirm that these illusions are harmless. There is no great cause for concern.

dialogue.sit: I see.
I'm glad that they weren't real.

dialogue.t: Hmm. All the mirage stories I've heard are either animals, rocks, or small houses. Abyssal monsters, though? That's a first.
It's a first for me, too, so I'm planning to look into it further just to be on the safe side. I intend to inspect a few more locations.
What about you two? Any plans?
Alice contacted me a few days ago. She'd like me and Durin to assist her with an experiment.
But we lost contact shortly after receiving the message. I'm sure that comes as no surprise to anyone familiar with her.
We don't know when the wind will blow, yet when the wind blows, we will know. That, in a nutshell, describes how Alice operates.
Yeah. That tracks.
Okay. Well, I suggest we investigate this mirage business in the meantime. It's piqued my curiosity, and I'm pretty sure I know someone who will already be ten steps ahead of us.
Hah, well said.
Right? Whatever's happening in Nod-Krai, she always seems to be the first one to know.
Let's go see what she knows. We can invite her and her staff to the festival while we're at it.
Goodbye for now. I look forward to the festival.
You're right, I have noticed. There's certainly something a little fishy about this situation. Only a little, though.
Records indicate that this phenomenon can occur in the days before and following Moon-Prayer Night. That said, it has always been a rare sight in the past.
The odds of encountering these phantoms are similar to looking up in the night sky, happening to see a shooting star, and managing to make a wish before it disappears.
But this time... either everyone's getting lucky, or they're appearing far more frequently than usual.
Jahoda's out gathering intel as we speak. In the meantime, let me check off some points of interest.
First, the Abyss.
The ones we saw seemed to be Abyssal monsters.
Indeed. But we have identified one location where many more of them have made an appearance. And not just monsters, but human phantoms, too.
Given the scale and nature of the phantoms, it's almost as if... someone's last memories are coming to life. Or perhaps the memories of multiple people.
Oh...
So you mean, the phantom monsters are hunting down the phantom humans?
Exactly. The phantoms can interact with each other, but we have no means of intervening.
In addition, some of the human phantoms would seem to be from the very distant past. This is clear both from the clothing they wear and the stories they tell.
They claim to be from Hyperborea — a name which I've heard from Lauma before. If this is true, it means they must be from 6,000 years ago...
Did Paimon hear that right? Six thousand years!?
It sounds like this merits further exploration.
That'd be a big help. I'll leave it with you, Albedo — my knowledge of ancient history is non-existent. I used to doze off every time the pre-Knights of Favonius era came up in class...
It's quite a miracle that you were able to understand these phantoms' speech, given how long ago they lived.
I suppose you're right. But I'll leave the archaeologists to ruminate over that conundrum. As an intelligence broker, my sole interest is in the value of the information I gather.
Which, in this case, hopefully means earning myself some good favor with our dear Lady Moonchanter.
So calculating... This intel broker logic always catches Paimon by surprise.
Sounds to me like we can split the work up.
I think the Abyssal phenomenon is best left to Albedo, Flins, and me.
Agreed. It coincides with my duty as a Lightkeeper.
For my part, I'd like to understand the Abyss better. Even a little knowledge would go a long way.
This is certainly a rare opportunity to study the Abyss. But even rarer, perhaps, is the chance to make contact with the ancients.
The Curatorium will take the lead on investigating the Hyperboreans. We put in the work to learn what we know so far — it seems only fair that we get some quantity of exclusive intel.
That just leaves our trusty team of two unassigned.

dialogue.sit: Seems like it, yeah.
Wait, we're a team? Since when?

dialogue.t: Since you became an Honorary Knight, of course. This was part of my grand plan all along, hahaha!
Oh yeah! By the way, we managed to convince Columbina to come to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations. Would you and Jahoda like to join too?
She agreed to that? Huh. Quite an achievement. Never underestimate {NICKNAME}, I guess.
I'd be happy to join. No point shutting myself inside when the streets are all decked out. I doubt any clients will be visiting during the festival in any case.
And Jahoda loves a party, so I'm sure she'll jump at the opportunity.
No, no, no no nonononono...
Tsk, way to contradict me in front of—
Wait, no! That's not what I... I have bad news, Boss!
So many people... Alright, everyone inside, quick!
This is gonna sound crazy, but hear me out... I saw one of those phantoms at Starsand Shoal, and it was... it was some sorta... flying ship!
Like a spaceship!?

dialogue.sit: A spaceship at Starsand Shoal...

dialogue.t: That's gotta be the one you came to Teyvat in. You said you saw the same thing through the Moon Marrow, right?
Huh? You already know about it? Ugh... And I thought it was gonna blow people's minds, turns out I'm the last to find out...
Wait, back up! You came here in a spaceship!? Now MY mind is blown. What's it like on the inside? What's it like flying through space? Ahhh, I wanna know everything!

dialogue.sit: M—Maybe that's a conversation for next time...
This is still a huge discovery on your part.

dialogue.t: Yep, exactly! Huuuge discovery! You're the best... uh, second-best intel-broker in the world! After your boss, of course.
W—Wow, really? Hehe, well, I dunno if I'm all that, but...
I guess that decides where we're heading next.
...Come on, don't look at me like that. I know the spaceship doesn't have anything to do with me, but... You don't wanna leave me as the only one twiddling my thumbs, do you? ...Please?
Eh, fair enough. You can tag along.
In that case, let's meet back here to discuss our findings once we're done.
I wish everyone a productive investigation.
You too!
*sigh*
What's up, Boss? Aren't we gonna head out?
Tell me, Jahoda. When did the Curatorium start giving out intel for free?
Oh, uh... S—Sorry, Boss!
Well, whaddya know? Jahoda was right on the money. This phantom really is your spaceship...
But that's so weird. Why would it show up here? Is it some kind of projection? Or... a ghost? Like, maybe it no longer exists, but somehow it left an afterimage...?

dialogue.sit: I'm not sure either...

dialogue.t: Ah, you're already here.
Miss Lauma, what a surprise. I thought you were busy with festival preparations?
I was, until one of our people informed me that a strange sight had appeared at Starsand Shoal.
No one's ever seen something quite like this before. I thought I should see it for myself.
Same here! Oh — so, we heard that these things appear around the festival period. Any idea why that is?
Unfortunately not. We have very limited information about them, since they can't be interacted with, and no human phantoms have ever made an appearance before now.
The most we've been able to deduce is that these sightings appear to be connected to the increase in kuuvahki energy around this time.

dialogue.sit: Let's look around and see what we can find out.

dialogue.t: Yeah. Seems like that's all we can do. This is all so confusing.
Allow me to lend you a hand.
We can't unshare information, any more than water spilled on sand can be put back in the bucket. I'll just have to balance the books some other way...
Please, Boss, there's gotta be another way... Who knows — depending on what they find, maybe this will work in our favor, hehe... Please don't fine me, pleeease!
Have you ever seen anything like this?
Nope. Never seen or heard anything this weird...
Those illusions, and those people... It's all a little creepy, don't you think?
Hahaha! Nah, all part of the festive atmosphere!
Everyone, our friend here should be able to provide us with some information.
Is that.... a phantom Rimehorn Deer...?
I've heard about how the Frostmoon Scions live in harmony with the animals, and can even communicate with them. That's coming in handy now, for sure.
Okay... yes, I understand... Then, how about this...
Oh, it's leaving...
It appears to share our curiosity about this giant spaceship, so I asked it if it wouldn't mind investigating along with some friends.
In return, I told it about some nearby spots where the wild fruit grows abundantly.
We may live in a different era from these phantoms, but I trust that the terrain, climate, and ecology here are more resistant to the effects of time than some things are.
Let's give them a moment, and hope for the best.

dialogue.sit: After a few moments, the Rimehorn Deer and its companions return happily.

dialogue.t: All back together? Must've been a lot of fruit.
Indeed. Now let me ask them some questions...
It did find a lot of wild fruit, enough for them to feast for a long while.
This puffin circled in the air several times, but didn't spot anything out of the ordinary. Certainly nothing to do with the spaceship.
Huh... Well, it definitely makes sense to get a bird's eye view.
Indeed. Other than that, I was also thinking that the world these phantoms see is also different from ours.
Oh, I get what you mean. The "wild fruit" exist in both times and spaces, but there might also be things that only exist in that space-time, which we can't see.

dialogue.sit: Because we don't see their whole world.
We only see small fragments.

dialogue.t: Good point... Great thinking, Lauma!
Blunthorn Rhinos can use kuuvahki to shift great rocks, but this one says it couldn't get that ship to budge by even an inch.
The Sniffer Mole tried too. But despite being a skilled digger, it could not get through.
They say that the spaceship looks robust and undamaged. It seems completely impervious to any and all attacks. Whatever lies within is well-defended from harm.
So, just like us humans, there was nothing they could do about this spaceship either.
Yes. Still, they deserve our thanks.
We are grateful for all your efforts, dear friends. Now go, and enjoy your feast.
I've noticed some other human phantoms gathered nearby. C'mon. Let's go talk to them.
What is this thing? I've never seen it move, and there's no way to get inside.
Goodness knows. My grandpa says it's been sitting here at least since his grandpa was still alive.
What about his grandpa? Did he say anything to your grandpa's grandpa about it?
Huh? Um... I don't know. In all likelihood, it was here back then too. Hard to imagine something this huge could move.
Hmm. Guess that means that as far as they're concerned, this ship's been around a long time.
Come on, brothers! If we can get even a small chunk off of this thing, it's gotta be worth a fortune! Today is the day we strike it rich!
Huh...? Y—You mean Paimon?
Yes, brother! I shall join you! Let's make our fortune!
...We should go with them.
What the... This thing is crazy tough, I can't even scratch it. What's it made of!?
Sorry, brother... Looks like we'll have to seek our fortunes elsewhere...
Enjoying yourself?
I was just seeing if I could influence this phantom's perception by playing — but nope. No dice.
I'm sure we're all starting to build up an idea of what's going on here now that we've spoken to some of the people.
These phantoms are reenacting real, historical events in Nod-Krai.
It's almost like we're in some kind of interactive stage play. We can talk to the actors, but the plot is fixed, and we can't influence it.
It makes sense. History is set in stone. The objective facts of the past cannot be changed.
Paimon totally thought you were just goofing around earlier... But actually, you were doing some serious investigating.
Of course I was. Anyway, at this point, I think we're forced to conclude that although the phantom spaceship is right there in front of us, we aren't gonna learn much about it from these people.

dialogue.sit: (If only this showed the moment when my sister(brother) was searching for me. Maybe then, I could've discovered why she(he) wasn't in the spaceship...)
(...Or, if it showed the moment when it disappeared, I might've found out who was piloting it, and where they were headed...)
(But no such luck. All we've seen is an arbitrary moment in time during its long stay here.)

dialogue.t: Don't be discouraged. If nothing else, this is proof of the ship's existence.
And think about it. So many people tried to hack their way inside, but no one could get the door open. It's made of very tough material.
To me, that says that we'll either find the ship itself, or the story behind it — it's just a matter of time.

dialogue.sit: Thanks, Varka.

dialogue.t: Huh, every now and then, when Varka gets serious, he actually does seem like Grand Master material for once...
I wonder how the others are doing... Let's head back for now.
Sounds good. Also, drinks are on me if Team Knights of Favonius is the first to finish.
Wait, we have a team name now...?
...Am I in "Team Knights of Favonius" as well?
You're very welcome to join. We've even got a cathedral ready for you!
Isn't that technically blasphemy? You wouldn't dare make a joke like that if Barbatos was in earshot...
Hahaha! Nah, I'm sure Barbatos doesn't mind a little harmless blasphemy once in a while.
Help!
Oh no! Get away!
Oh...
Aaaaaaggghhh!
I know it's hard to stomach, Mr. Durin. But as I'm sure you've noticed, there is nothing we can do to intervene in that which unfolds before us.
*panting* But... we have to at least try...
And try you have. But are you aware of how many unsuccessful attempts you've made now?
Uh... I wasn't keeping count...
I'm afraid this is the thirty-ninth failure so far. Or the fifth, if we're only counting this particular victim.
There are no indications that these phantoms may be altered in any way.
You seem to have calmed down a little.
I'll make us a fire. You should rest and have some water.
Feeling any better now, Mr. Durin?
...May I ask a few questions?
Be my guest.
What exactly are we witnessing here? What happened to those people?
My guess would be that we are seeing Nod-Krai during the Khaenri'ahn Cataclysm. Would that be accurate?
Khaenri'ah...
That is correct.
As you know, once the Abyss senses even the tiniest crack, it floods in and spreads like wildfire.
There was a time in the distant past when it permeated all of Nod-Krai, causing immeasurable harm. The people paid a terrible price to heal this land.
Then, five hundred years ago, the whole of Teyvat suffered an Abyssal disaster. Once more, Nod-Krai was dealt a devastating blow.
I see...
In the face of the Abyssal onslaught, all were like grains of sand tossed around by a tidal wave, be they human, fae, or god.
The moment you witnessed is but one drop in a whole ocean of catastrophe.
Alright... I guess that answers my second question, too. I wanted to know why there's nothing I could do to help them — and that's because what we are seeing is history.
That would be my guess as well.
As I understand it, history and fate are not all that dissimilar. The latter may be unseen to us, but both are immutable.
Yes, fate was determined long, long ago.
I still have a couple of other questions for you, Mr. Flins...
You mentioned more than one Abyssal disaster that has struck this land in the past. How can you be sure that what we're seeing is from the Khaenri'ahn incident?
And also... how are you able to stay so calm when you're talking about these events?
From everything I know about you, you're not cold or ruthless, and you're not indifferent to the suffering of others...
Hmph... Alas, I am forced to show my age. I must be six or seven hundred years old by human measure.
Wait... So you...
One is not easily moved by history when one has witnessed the truth firsthand.
I'm sorry.
You needn't apologize. Your passion is a good thing to have. Treasure it, because someday, you may find it in terribly short supply.
Now, at the risk of offending you, I have a question in return...
Your curiosity toward the Abyss — is it born from hatred, or because you sense its call?
I only ask because I kept a fragment of Rerir's body in my lantern for a short time — specifically, his heart. So, I know what a burden it can be to carry the Abyss with you.
And I hear its power growling from somewhere within you. In my eyes, your mere existence is a miracle.
My honest answer is... I don't know. I don't think I have the confidence to say for certain. What I will say is, the Abyss is not the only issue that haunts me.
Even before I became who I am today, the question dogged me constantly... should I even exist at all?
My doubts remain unresolved. But... when we fought Rerir, something became a little clearer to me...
Sometimes, it is the darkness within us that allows us to achieve the impossible.
I certainly got the sense from your thirty-nine attempts that you were trying to achieve the impossible.
It sounds like you've resolved to see the truth for yourself.
Absolutely. In that sense, he and I are quite similar.
Then I wish you every success. I look forward to the day of your transcension.
Well, if everyone's caught their breath, I suppose we should head back. Oh, and one last thing... I'd appreciate if you kept our discussion about history a secret.
Incredibly, our separate investigations led us all to the same conclusion. Hooray for consensus.
Yeah, but we barely learned anything though... I totally thought this would be the motherlode! Talking with the ancients? I mean, come on! But nope, all we got was useless snippets of conversation...
And all this stuff about moons, and "hyberorpea"? What a load of baloney. Seems like people back then had a few screws loose.
I understand your frustration. We found the same issue — each phantom only showed a very brief moment in time.
There isn't much value to be found in these miscellaneous fragments of a civilization's history, no matter how glorious it may have been.
If there's a silver lining, it's that these phantoms are harmless to the present reality. They shouldn't get in the way of the festivities.
Paimon agrees! And not just because it's the first thing she understood in this whole conversation.
You look disappointed, Nefer. Is something the matter?
What do you think? We all worked our tails off, but the only one to gain anything from it was you, Lady Moonchanter.
Well, please do share the Hyperborean records with me. I will gladly inscribe them in our people's documents.
Oh, duh, yeah, that was it! Hyperborea, Hyperborea...
I'm serious. Only an expert in the Frostmoon Scions and their history can turn these records into valuable research material.
The alternative is to let them gather dust on the Curatorium's storage shelves until the pages turn yellow.
Nefer, you're wise enough to know that cooperating and sharing the profits is the best course of action here.
Well, that goes without saying. Sure, let's do that.
Huh? But didn't you say we aren't supposed to give out intel for free..? Aaah, sorry! Shutting up, shutting up!
Now is not a good time to push Nefer's buttons...
Haha. Anyway, back to Moon-Prayer Night. I'm thinking that we should prepare something a little special, aside from the usual decorations and so on.
You mean, a parting gift?
Can't go wrong with food! Although... Hmm, does food go bad on the moon?
Perhaps a lantern would be a better choice. It might be dark up there.
Mm... It could prove difficult to light a lantern on the moon. Magical stones might serve that purpose better.
What about a clockwork meka model from Fontaine? I've got a whole bunch at home. I use 'em for fighting practice in my free time!
None of these sound like things she would be even remotely interested in. But we don't interact with her enough to know what she likes...
Yeah. It would really save us the guesswork if someone could find out what she's into.
Wait, what the... Uh, {NICKNAME}, they're all looking at you!

dialogue.sit: Okay, I got it...
I'll find a chance to ask her.

dialogue.t: Great! Haha, problem solved. Now, I need to stop by Dori's. Gonna need her help sourcing a bunch of stuff for the festival.
Then let's leave it there for now. We all have our own business to attend to. {NICKNAME} — if you find out what Kuutar likes, let us know right away.

dialogue.sit: Gotcha.

dialogue.t: Is something the matter?

dialogue.sit: That's my line, Durin.
You seem a little down.

dialogue.t: Ah, I'm fine. It's just... I'm still feeling a little rattled after witnessing the horrors of the Abyss.
But it's okay. This is something I have to work through... I'll be alright. Thanks for your concern.
Well, don't put too much pressure on yourself. If you ever feel like something's wrong, physically or mentally, we're here to talk.

dialogue.sit: Don't forget, I'm a member of the Knights of Favonius.
You can always rely on me.

dialogue.t: Hah, come on, stop treating me like a kid.

quests.description: The journey so far has reached a brief pause. Take a moment to rest and check in on your companions.

quests.title: Ripples That Will Never Reach

dialogue.t: Columbina! We're back!
...Huh. She's not here.

dialogue.sit: I can't sense her presence at all.

dialogue.t: Weren't there a few kuuhenki here last time, too? Where did they all go?

dialogue.sit: Maybe she took them out for walkies?

dialogue.t: Uh... Walkies? For kuuhenki? They're not pets, you know...
Oh well, looks like we just came at a bad time. Let's try again tomorrow.
There's still a few days until Moon-Prayer Night, so we're in no rush. Besides, she needs time to rest anyway.

dialogue.sit: Fair point. Let's go.

dialogue.t: Columbina? Are you back yet?
Huh. How strange. Looks like she still isn't here.

dialogue.sit: This is a bit odd...

dialogue.t: Right? It's not like her to spend so much time outside. Especially since she's worried about attracting unwanted attention.

dialogue.sit: By the looks of it, she hasn't been back all day.

dialogue.t: What about Luonnotar? Luonnotar, you there?
Hey! Do you know where Columbina went?
...Sorry, didn't understand. But if you know where she is, could you take us to her?

dialogue.sit: Sounds like an "I don't know either" to me.

dialogue.t: Yeah... That's even stranger...

dialogue.sit: Paimon, look...
The flowers...

dialogue.t: What about 'em? Oh... That's not good news...
They change color when Columbina gets weaker, right? And they look super pale right now...

dialogue.sit: Let's go. We've got to find Lauma.

dialogue.t: Good idea. She might know what's happening.
Lauma!
Ah, it's you. How is Kuutar? Is she okay?

dialogue.sit: She's missing.
Has she visited the Frostmoon Scions?

dialogue.t: No, she hasn't... I came here to check on her after I noticed the flowers had changed color.
Based on past precedent, she must be very weak right now. Even getting up to walk would be a struggle... it seems unlikely that she wandered off outside.
Not to mention that she doesn't do that at the best of times, either. So yeah, this is super weird.

dialogue.sit: Has anyone approached Silvermoon Hall lately?

dialogue.t: No. Very few people are in the know about Kuutar's whereabouts. And if anyone suspicious had visited, they'd have left some sort of evidence.
Come on, let's go to Nasha Town. If anyone has seen her, someone there will know about it. It's Nod-Krai's information hub after all.
Makes sense. Let's go!
You should get going. It's important that we ascertain what Kuutar likes.
Miss Lauma, would you accompany me into town? I think it'd be best if you saw the Frostmoon Scions' decorations for yourself.
Very well. Let's go.

dialogue.sit: After leaving the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]} goes to meet Durin and Albedo, who are observing the phantoms.

dialogue.t: Could you do me a solid and try to smooth things over with Boss Nef?
...Which is why we need a lantern guaranteed to work on the moon.
Yes. I have a few ideas, but... The lantern itself is the easy part. The real issue is how little we know about the lunar environment.
Wait... you two are serious about this?
Hehe. Let's just say I'm intrigued by these shining magical stones that Mr. Albedo has mentioned.
Are you out for a walk too?
n/a
Oh...
The day has come at last...
n/a

dialogue.sit: n/a

dialogue.t: Wait a moment... Is it just Paimon, or is this stall kinda suspicious? It's never been here before, right?
No... I don't recognize it...
Mwahahaha! Alas, your free-and-easy adventure time is over. Now, prepare to face the final boss of Nod-Krai!
Whoa! Where'd that voice come from?
Not sure, but it's definitely hostile...
No, no, no, not that way! The final boss is right here.
The... Sniffer Mole?
That's the final boss? Surely not. Also...

dialogue.sit: That voice is a little familiar.

dialogue.t: Hahaha, okay, the jig is up. I'll stop teasing you. Turn around — I'm right behind you.
It seems I've managed to leave quite an indelible impression, even though you've never seen my face... Ah, nothing could make a great mage more pleased with herself.
Wh—What is going on...
I've heard that all the big shots of Teyvat have long, wordy titles that stun people speechless when they make their entrance.

Unfortunately, none of them are affiliated with the Hexenzirkel, and we ourselves keep a very low profile... The notorious name-dropping doesn't quite work for us. Still, I for one think I'm really quite amazing.
So that didn't stop me from coming up with a title anyway.
Alice? It's really you this time! Not a lantern, or a Dodoco... but Alice in the flesh!
That's right! So, what do you think? How does it feel to finally meet me?
You... You look like...

dialogue.sit: You look just like Klee!
You look so young!

dialogue.t: Aha! That's the first thing you thought? A little surprising, but that actually makes me very happy.
Because that means that when Klee grows up, she'll be just as stunningly beautiful as her mother!
So, she's a... friend of yours?
Uhh... Kind of? This is actually the first time we've seen her in person.
I see. Madame Mage, that was, uh... quite a powerful entrance. I certainly won't be forgetting it any time soon...
It's okay, Lauma, don't force it. Paimon will do the honors. This is Alice from the Hexenzirkel. She's a friend of ours, and of Varka's too.

dialogue.sit: She's helped us a lot in the past.

dialogue.t: That's right! She's a good person, just kinda... unpredictable.
Well, what is the human heart if not unpredictable, hmm? If we could not do as we please, how would we differ from machines?
I am Lauma, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions. It is a pleasure to meet you.
Oh, I know, I know. Before you got here, I spent a good, oh, 15 minutes getting up to speed on Nod-Krai's present situation.
In other words, I've read the whole "in the last episode" part, so we can skip the pleasantries.
Fair enough. Well, Ms. Alice, I can already tell that you have quite a unique personality.
You'll get used to it. Paimon sure is... So anyway, what are you doing in Nod-Krai, Alice?
Oh? I thought I told you already? This time, I'm the final boss.
And what a formidable foe I shall be! Powerful, confident, decisive! And good luck finding my weak spot — you will never succeed!

dialogue.sit: I'm going to send a formal request for Jean to put you in solitary.

dialogue.t: *gasp* Ah! Drat! My one weakness, and you found it in an instant! Fate has been dealt a devastating blow...
Thus falls the great Dodo-King!
...Uh, why are you playing along with this nonsense?
For funsies, of course! What's wrong, Paimon? Are you disappointed in me? Am I a gigantic let-down?
No, no, it's just... You seem like a busy lady, and this is the one time you've shown up in person. Paimon figured it would be for something more high-stakes than just goofing around...
You're quite right. I'm here in Nod-Krai because something big happened. Something big enough that it caught the attention of the Hexenzirkel.
It concerns the three moons, Teyvat's borders, and of course, the Moon Goddess you are currently searching for.

dialogue.sit: You know where Columbina is?

dialogue.t: Kind of. Why don't we discuss this over a pot of tea?
My main reason for coming on this trip to Teyvat was, of course, to have some fun. But I do technically have a job to do as well — namely, maintaining the stability of Teyvat's borders.
I'll skip over the complicated parts, but to sum it up, Abyssal energies are all that lie beyond Teyvat's border. We'd find ourselves in a real pickle if they ever made it through.
And the phantoms you've been seeing are a sign that the border has been disturbed.
Ah, no wonder they tend to show up around Moon-Prayer Night...
Is it because the real moon is now so close to us that its power can cross the border?
In part. But only a negligible amount passes through — just enough to influence the Verdant Crests and so on.

And as you've noticed, there has been an unprecedented number of phantoms appearing this year. The influence of the moon beyond the border cannot explain this. No, there is another, far greater factor at play...
The "Trilunar Syzygy."
A Trilunar... Syzygy...
Eons ago, before the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat, it was the then-three Moon Goddesses who controlled the laws of this world.

dialogue.sit: You're talking about...
Life, "Death," and such, aren't you?

dialogue.t: That's exactly it. The three goddesses split these powers amongst themselves, promising never to consolidate them into one singular body. This was meant to keep the world stable.

But fast-forwarding to the present, the Eternal Moon's Marrow is with you, while the Iridescent Moon's Marrow — which should never have appeared in this world — has been retrieved. Add that to the presence of a Moon Goddess in the flesh, and...
The power of all three moons is gathered here in Nod-Krai. There hasn't been an event like this since the war of funerary flame.
And it's having a noticeable effect on Teyvat's borders.

dialogue.sit: Why are you so concerned about said borders, if I might ask?

dialogue.t: Because... I wish to give my darling daughter a peaceful, sunny environment to grow up in. Is that a good enough reason?
Kinda sounds like you're dodging the question... but it does make sense.
Well, that's one reason, anyway. And the most important one. The others are a little complicated to explain — for instance, cleaning up after dearest Miss "R"...
Albedo can tell you more about that if you're curious. But right now, I have a more important question to ask you: Why are you collecting the Moon Marrows?

dialogue.sit: Columbina wants to use their power to return home.

dialogue.t: I see, I see. Nicole told me about that legend once.
N—Nicole!? You mean Mage "N"?
Oh, so you remember.

dialogue.sit: We heard her voice in Fontaine...

dialogue.t: Ah yes, of course. That was a story about "fate" — her area of expertise.
But back to the story of our dear Moon Goddess... I'm afraid her intended method of returning to the moon is unlikely to work anymore.
What does that mean?
She may be missing... but she hasn't "gone" anywhere. She has... disappeared.
My body is so... heavy...
(Wait, no. It's... my mind that's heavy. My arms and legs are as light as a feather...)
(What's... happening to me? I feel... drowsy, like I've been asleep for too long... Is it daytime or nighttime? Is the moon out?)
Phew... I think I'll go for a walk.
Have I grown so weak that... I can't even sustain my physical form?
But Moon-Prayer Night is nearly here... I was so close to returning home...
Death is near... Is this how it ends for me...?
(Will I return to the moon after I disappear? Or...)
*sigh*... I don't want it to end like this.
(So far, at least, I still exist — even if not physically. I can still feel...)
(But as my power wanes, I'm sure that, too, will fade...)
I suppose... I might take one final look at this world. The world where I was born.
...Hahahaha! Come on, come on!
...Wait for meeee!
The Frostmoon Enclave... How much it has changed since I was born...
These decorations... they're so heavy!
It's times like this when you kinda wish men could be priestesses and acolytes too...
(How fascinating... I've never had the chance to be privy to people's private lives in this way.)
(In the past, people would get so solemn and serious the moment I showed my face... like they were frozen stiff.)
Kaarina! Lemetti! It's time to eat!
Coming!
(...I want to watch them a little longer.)
I'm sure you're both tired from playing all day! Come on, eat up.
(...A plain, humble meal. That has always been the way of the Frostmoon Scions.)
Huh? How come Lemetti got a Midsommar Berry dessert? I always get Lakkaberry...
Umm... I don't mind sharing! You can have a bite of mine if I get to have a bite of yours?
(Hmm? They're sharing food?)
(I've never shared food with anyone before... Even at the Harbinger tea parties, everyone just ate off their own plate...)
(And when I couldn't finish my food offerings from the Frostmoon Scions, they'd leave the leftovers out under the moonlight for the animals to claim...)
Hey! That was two bites!
Oh, uh... Then you can have another bite of mine!
Oh, you two...
Don't fret, now. Here, have some of Granny's, too.
Hehe... So this is what it means to be "family"?
...So just, fill these balloons with air, right?
Yep. Try a couple now to test things out — the rest can wait till Moon-Prayer Night.
...Hehehe.
Think fast!
Aah!
Reettaaaa!
(Teasing an acolyte of the Frostmoon Scions? Surely that's a punishable offense...)
Take THIS!
Ahahaha!
...Huh?
Heh! Alright, enough horsing around. Lady Lauma gave us a task — we should get back to it.
The task is just to check that the balloons don't leak, right? Doesn't matter if we fill them with air or water. Hi-yah!
Oof! Okay, you got me there... Aaand you got me there. But still, we can't use all the balloons before the festival even starts.
We won't use ALL of them... And as long as Lady Lauma's trusted acolyte doesn't snitch, this can stay as a little secret between friends. A couple more can't do any harm, right?
Oh, you menace... Then THINK FAST!
Hahaha!
...Is pumping a balloon full of water really so much fun?
(I'm seeing so much that I'd never usually get to see... They'd never act like this when I was around.)
(Mmm... It's nice, being able to just watch people in peace in these final moments...)
What a rare opportunity. I think I'll go take a look around in Nasha Town, too. Maybe {NICKNAME} will be there...
After the war of funerary flame, the Moon Goddesses were no longer recognized by Teyvat. They lost the whole foundation for their existence.
That's why the Moon Goddess's strength is fading. She cannot withstand the world's rejection of her.

dialogue.sit: It's just like what Columbina said...
The world itself is rejecting her...

dialogue.t: To be more pedantic about it, the Moon Goddesses did something to offend the Heavenly Principles, and that's why they were ousted. Something of a recurring theme in Teyvat's history.
Theoretically, speaking so candidly should put me in their crosshairs, too — but they can't tell me what to do. I'll say whatever I want.
Anywho, the Moon Marrow energies were but a drop in the bucket for her, and that battle against the Rächer of Solnari only weakened her further.
Fortunately, it happened close enough to Moon-Prayer Night, when the kuuvahki concentration here is high. That's the only reason she's managed to survive this long.
What do you mean, "fortunately"? You said she disappeared... We're too late...
Ugh, what a headache — I thought this was all common knowledge. I guess I have some more explaining to do... Okay, buckle up, it's time for another lecture.
Now, I said earlier that the Moon Goddesses lost the foundation for their existence.
The reason for that has to do with the natural order. Basically, the rationale for their existence in Teyvat was lost.
The same logic applies to the present Moon Goddess, too. Consider her existence so far. Her comrades in the Fatui called her "Damselette"...
And she was worshiped as Kuutar by the Frostmoon Scions. But these connections have now been severed, whether by her hand or yours.
So the "rationale" that once sustained her existence is now gone...
Wait... we did that to her!?
Well, strictly speaking... yes, but let's not start pointing fingers, shall we? I'll only end up as the big bad villain, and that's not the kind of final boss I want to be!

dialogue.sit: If you're making light of this...
Hopefully that means you have a plan?

dialogue.t: Of course I do! I'm only the greatest mage in the whole entire world!
Now, if you wish to find your Moon Goddess, there are two problems we need to solve.
Firstly, we'll need to strengthen the connection between her and Teyvat, at least enough to sustain her until Moon-Prayer Night.
Strengthen her connection... But... does that mean I'll have to rally all the Frostmoon faithful behind this?
I'm afraid a bygone faith and a former home won't be of any help to her now. Hmm... Do you know her name?
Her... name?
Yes. Names are very important things. A name is a fundamental concept that anchors one's entire existence.

dialogue.sit: I asked her once, but she said she didn't know.

dialogue.t: Then your first job is to find it. As a Moon Goddess, I'm sure she must have a name she identifies with.
Neither "Columbina" nor "Kuutar" is her true name, and she's never really accepted either of them.
So... finding out her real name is enough to sustain her existence?
Yes. I know it sounds like a small step, but every journey begins that way. So for now, that's all we need to focus on.
The second problem is with her plan to use the Moon Marrows to return to the moon. Unfortunately, piercing through the false sky will take an enormous amount of power.
Given her current condition, she won't be able to provide anywhere near enough power — even if she recovers her physical form.
But, no need to fret. Nicole's the expert in this field, and I'm sure she'll figure something out.
Wait, Mage "N" is going to help us out, too?
That means we've got two Hexenzirkel mages on the case... This is turning into a pretty big deal!
Mm... Actually, this is more of a side quest for me. Hehe.
Like you said, I'm a busy lady, so I can't stay for too long. I'll have to return to Teyvat's border soon.

dialogue.sit: Thanks for telling us all of this.

dialogue.t: Haha, that's the upside you get for looking out for my little Klee! Hopefully that will incentivize you to carry on keeping her company in the future~
Anyway, jokes aside, you'd better get moving. It will take quite a miracle for the Moon Goddess's consciousness to hold out till Moon-Prayer Night.
Oh! And I suppose I might as well tell you where Nicole is before I leave.
Off you go, now! Time to meet your new friend. Ah yes, and a little suggestion — don't forget to... mind your heads.
Uhh... What?
Hmm, I wonder how Durin's doing? I should really go see him before I head back.
You really are super busy.
*sigh* I most certainly am! There's so many children I have to keep tabs on just in Mondstadt. Durin, Albedo, Venti, Varka...

dialogue.sit: There were some unexpected names in there.

dialogue.t: Klee didn't make the list, huh?
Of course not. Klee is my pride and joy. I have no qualms about her, because she's the best child in the whole wide world.
Oh... Uh, yep! Klee's a little angel, mm-hmm...
I'm glad you agree. Well, all the best! See you when I see you~
She left in a hurry.
Yeah, she didn't pack up her stall. Should we handle it for her?

dialogue.sit: I doubt that's necessary.
A mage of her abilities doesn't need our help.

dialogue.t: I must say, I'm now very curious about her daughter... Klee, wasn't it? What's she like?
That's... a long story. Come on, we'll fill you in as we go.
(What a lively place. I've never experienced Nasha Town like this before.)
Hey, you old geezer. Your hammer's rusted through!
Who are you calling "old geezer"?
(Are they... quarreling?)

I'm lookin' right at him! You've really gone downhill since giving your daughter free reign in the workshop. Can you even swing a hammer anymore? It shouldn't take you days just to fix a single chair!
You might as well use that hammer to massage my back, for all the good it's doing!

Heh, don't run your mouth, or you'll get a back massage that'll put you in bed for the rest of your life! Look, the materials haven't arrived yet, alright? You know how busy it gets in the days before Moon-Prayer Night!
I'll bet you sent all the materials to your little princess. *sigh* Blood's always thicker than water, huh?

Alright, you've made your point, Uncle Koski. As soon as the materials arrive, fixing your chair will be the number one priority. And dad, if you've got time to chat, why don't you lend me a hand, hmm?
See? Lyulka knows what the score is.
(I guess they're... friends? But the way they spoke to each other was so ugly.)
(Then again... It wouldn't be the first time I've seen something like this...)
Columbinaaaa! Sing outside my door in the middle of the night one more time and I'll unscrew your vocal cords! You hear me?
Oh... Sandrone...
(So that was her way of trying to be friends with me?)
What a pity... I won't get the chance to say any ugly things in reply...
...Hey, have you decided what to give her for Moon-Prayer Night?
I sure have! Hehe, she's gonna get the surprise of her life when she's least expecting it! Then I'll whip out the ring and pop the question...
("The surprise of her life"... What a fun turn of phrase.)
Cool, I get the picture. You can spare me the gushy details... Oh! Looks like we have a customer.
Hello there, Ma'am. Would you like some Moon-Prayer Night candy?
...Huh?
(Is he... talking to me? Can he see me?)
Here you go!
Oh...
Come back any time! Right, now where were we...
I don't know why but... I still held out hope...
...The most important thing right now is to find that mage...
...This name thing seems super important too. But where do we even start looking?
...I'd better go pay the Fatui a visit...

dialogue.sit: Columbina?

dialogue.t: {NICKNAME}?
Let's go. This is no time to be spacing out.
(Where are they going? They mentioned a "mage" and... a name?)
So, Mr. Varka, are you acquainted with this Nicole? Or should I call her Mage "N"?
Ah, not really. We've never met, though she has come up in conversation.
From what I've gathered, Alice kinda took Nicole under her wing. Taught her how to speak in a more ladylike fashion, that kind of thing.
Huh... Hard to imagine Alice as an etiquette coach...
Haha! Yeah, Alice is a larger-than-life personality, I'll give you that. But then again, that's why she's able to draw such an eclectic mix of people into her inner circle.
If I remember correctly, being an "interesting" person is actually one of her main entry requirements. Heh, so if you ever wanted to join the Hexenzirkel, I'm sure you'd both be eligible to apply.
Hey, don't go around making promises on Alice's behalf.
I wouldn't dare! I'm just... trying to paint a picture of the Hexenzirkel for you...
Okay, sure. Anyway, since none of us have ever met Nicole, how are we supposed to find her? We can't just go up to every woman in sight and ask, "Hey, are you Nicole?"
Hmm, maybe something she's wearing will give it away? Like, uh, a Windblume pinned to her chest, or something.
Wait a minute. Alice never said Nicole was from Mondstadt.
...Oh, true.

dialogue.sit: What about a tea set?
I recall that each mage has their own cup.

dialogue.t: That would be... this young lady, then?
Hey there, sorry to disturb you, but... are you Ms. Nicole?
Varka, Knight of Boreas of the Knights of Favonius. Alice might have mentioned me before.
Uhh... Have we got the wrong person? Sorry, sorry!
(Well, this is awkward...)
When I shook my head, I meant "no, Alice hasn't mentioned you before."
Huh? Where is this voice coming from...?
My apologies. For certain reasons, I am unable to speak. This is the only way I can communicate with you.
It might take some getting used to, but I hope you can understand.
Hey, it's fine... I'm more shocked by the fact that Alice never speaks about me! Hahaha.
As for you two... We have crossed paths twice before, but it is nonetheless a pleasure to finally meet you.
It's really you! Thanks for all your guidance in the past...
You're quite welcome. This time, things are different... We have reached the unwritten pages of the story. You might say that we stand at the crossroads of fate...
Now, then. Allow me to formally introduce myself. My name is—
No no no, stop, I...! Ugh, Alice! I can't believe it...
I had a whole speech prepared! I'd agonized over every single word! ...She always picks the worst moments to ruin other people's plans...
I'm so sorry about that... Alice took the liberty of devising some bespoke "Self Introduction Magic" for each member of the Hexenzirkel...
But I could've sworn I deleted all of the triggering conditions for it. How did it bypass everything? ...Oh gosh, this is so embarrassing...
(This is a very different side of Nicole than what we're used to... Is she... not used to face-to-face interactions?)
Uh, d—don't worry about it. We've seen that introduction magic once already, so it wasn't too much of a shock.
Please go on, Ms. Nicole. We'd love to hear what you have to... say, or... well, communicate.
(Huh? Are they talking to this lady? But...)
Will you all promise to forget that horrendously embarrassing introduction?
Sorry? Embarrassing? When?

dialogue.sit: Among the words that hopped out just now, I saw...
Angel.

dialogue.t: ...Yes. My name is Nicole, and I am one of a very few angels who have retained both their preferred form and their power.
{NICKNAME} and Paimon should be no strangers to this concept. There is another of our kind in Natlan — they call her the Lord of the Night.
Ah, right, Paimon remembers her!

dialogue.sit: But we've never seen her in person.

dialogue.t: Yes, well, I have retained more of my power than she. It's because I don't have a long-term duty to fulfill. To be more specific...
...Ah, no, we'll be here all day if I get into the specifics. Moving on. If I'm not mistaken... you are here because you wish to learn how one might reach the moon beyond the sky.
That's right. Is that something you can give us any guidance on?
Yes, I do know a way. It began with the Hyperboreans who lived after the war of funerary flame... Hmm. Blank looks. Maybe I should start with the background of the war...
...Or maybe not. It shouldn't be an issue. I'll fill in the gaps for you when we have more time. Anyway, after that war ended, the three moons retreated to beyond the false sky.
The Hyperboreans were humans I once aided. They accepted the civilization and creations bestowed upon them by the angels.
But despite accepting many blessings of the angels, many among them still held onto their faith in the moons. They were reluctant to accept the new order.
Even after the war of funerary flame, they sought to contact the moon goddesses beyond the sky and receive their guidance...
But all three had passed away by that point.
(This mage has a unique method of communicating... Is she talking about the moons?)
Yes, but they did not know. And so, still they prayed for the Moon Goddesses' mercy.
After building titanic structures that consumed vast amounts of kuuvahki, at last they glimpsed the moons and heard their voices...
But of course, they were gravely disappointed. For it was then that they realized: the three moon goddesses were dead.
That's such a sad story...
It is. Humanity was in a very sorry state at that time. The angels who had once aided them were gone, and the war of funerary flames had left them homeless and destitute...
Just a second. I gotta ask... How relevant is all this history to the task at hand...?
Well, I mean, it's... Hmm. Okay, it seems we've drifted into irrelevant narrative waters.
It's been a while since I've had the chance to speak inside someone's head. As soon as I got started, I lost control, and the words just flowed out like a waterfall...
...What I'm trying to say is... Right, yes, that's it: The relevant part is the ritual created by the Hyperboreans.
The fact that they bypassed the false sky and saw the true moons implies that they successfully built a connection between Teyvat and the outside world.
Which means, with enough kuuvahki and a sufficiently stable connection, it should be feasible to send one person over the border.
Okay... so they built some kinda portal?
Oh, uh... Yes, a portal. Yes.
...Is something wrong? You sound... disappointed.
I just didn't expect you to summarize it so well... It turns out I could have said all that in one word, if only I'd managed to think of it.
No, please, it's fine. This is invaluable knowledge. I'll be sure to record and preserve everything in writing.
Oh, really? Well in that case, I suppose I could backtrack and add some more detail. I did gloss over a few things so far...
Whoa, whoa, whoa. Timeout. Let's summarize what we've got first!
The Hyperboreans were the last ones to use this method, right? So we somehow need to find whatever structure they built and make sure there's enough kuuvahki to power it up.
Luckily, we have the moon marrow of both the Eternal and Iridescent Moons, so we're all good for kuuvahki. Which means, the key issue we need to focus on is finding the place. Am I right so far?
Yes, although I expect the structure is long gone by now.
That said, what if we could take advantage of the phantoms to travel back to a time when it still existed?
Well, "travel back" isn't quite accurate. It's more like we'd be creating a handshake between two points in spacetime.

We wouldn't even have to pick a time when it still existed — it could just be a time when it still appeared in phantom form via projection. Or, we could project our own phantoms, fold them together, and...
...You look lost. Was that too hard to follow?
Yeah, things got a little, uh, technical there. Paimon's brain is reaching capacity...
Alright, let me think about how to put this more simply... Okay, got it.
Over the next few days, I'll search for phantoms that we can use. Once I find one that meets the criteria, I'll let you know and we'll regroup.
By completing certain rituals, specific individuals will be able to enter the phantom and make it to the Hyperborean structure.

If everything checks out, and it looks feasible, we'll just need to wait for Moon-Prayer Night and we can send the Moon Goddess back home... I'm really skimping on the detail here. Is this making any sense at all?
I think so. For now, we'll just wait to hear from you.
Yes... Basically, yes.
Great. Counting on you! In the meantime, we'll focus on finding the Moon Goddess's name.
(...! My... name? Are they... looking for a way to stop me from disappearing?)
Excuse me, Miss...
Go on, Ms. Nicole.
This conversation was a little all over the place. I didn't catch your name.
I am Lauma, of the Frostmoon Scions.
Ah, I did wonder. I noticed that you listened very intently when I spoke about Hyperborea and the moons' history.
If you'd be interested, I'd love to visit you this evening and go through it again in greater detail.

Also, if you were serious about making a record... It would be too risky to simply write down the raw details as-is. I would suggest some tweaks — maybe rewrite the stories as fairy tales or fables, perhaps even prayers.
...Anyway, we can cross that bridge when we come to it. So, see you later, then? Oh, and no need to prepare anything. Just a cup of tea will do.
S—See ya...
She seems friendly... it's just...

Ah, it's so nice to find someone who's actually willing to listen! I've been dying for a chance to finally go through all this systematically, from start to finish... Any longer and I'd probably start forgetting it!
Now Paimon gets why Alice told us to mind our heads...
Hahaha, what did I tell you? Lotta quirky people in Alice's orbit.
Now then, the next order of business is: Where do we start looking for the Moon Goddess's name?
Hmm... Maybe the rest of what Nicole has to say might give us some clues.
Once I've heard her out, I'll summarize the salient points and share them with you all.
I'm also inclined to review our other documents. Yes, our faith was first established by our Hyperborean ancestors...
But many of the more factually accurate records are from after Kuutar's birth.

dialogue.sit: I have a hunch that the Fatui might know something, too.

dialogue.t: Sounds like we're gonna follow Columbina's journey through Teyvat, huh?
In that case, we'll start by heading to the Frostmoon Enclave.
Sounds like a plan. Take this with you — I'll see about getting in touch with the Fatui... it'll probably just be Arlecchino and Sandrone again. They're the only ones who would wanna help.
Thank you, Mr. Varka.
Hahaha, don't mention it. Honestly, I'm more comfortable dealing with the Fatui than prying into the details of a young lady's childhood. Catch you later!
(I should follow them, just in case there's some way that I can help...)
A while ago, I took the time to organize all documents in our possession that pertain to Kuutar. What you see here is the material I consider reliable.
You're saying, there's unreliable material too?

Yes. Most of the information we have was transmitted through an oral tradition. Inevitably, some of her stories were mythologized and deified over the years through countless retellings. That's why I organized them into reliable and unreliable.
There is no sense seeking answers in history unless we can ensure the veracity of the historical record.
Makes sense. Alright, let's take a look through.

dialogue.sit: Clear and concise would be one way to describe the writing style of these historical records. But you could just as easily describe them as "terse and dry."
And since Lauma already knows the material like the back of her hand, the quest to find any new information in these texts is tough going.

dialogue.t: Almost all these records refer to "Kuutar" instead of "Columbina"... Hmm, although neither of those is her real name... Paimon's not sure what point she's trying to make.
What we can gather from these records is that the Frostmoon Scions worshiped her as a god, placing impossible expectations upon her...
I cannot fault them for their earnest faith. But for all their devotion, worshiping her day in, day out changed nothing.
I imagine that none of it resonated with Columbina.
It wouldn't surprise me if even back then, she had already begun to reject the name "Kuutar" and everything it represented...
(...Lauma speaks the truth.)
(When I heard them call upon "Kuutar" with hope and expectation in their voices... They may as well have been calling upon somebody else.)

dialogue.sit: When you were organizing these texts...
What criteria did you use?

dialogue.t: Well... That's a bit complicated. I looked at the level of detail, perceived authenticity, prose style...
And how realistic their portrayal of Kuutar seemed to be.
Amongst the Frostmoon Scions of today, only I know of her existence, and I alone have spoken to her face-to-face. As such, I know that there are certain things she simply would never do.
That being said, I have sensed some changes in her lately.
(...Changes? Me?)
Ugh, seems like this is getting us nowhere... For what it's worth, why don't we check the "unreliable" sources too?
Sure. Give me a moment.

Exerting but a fraction of her divine might, Kuutar sheared a great mass from the snow-capped mountain and cast it into the sea, upon whose surface shone the mirror image of the moon. Thus was formed the island of Hiisi.
Hehe...
Yeah, right... That doesn't even begin to pass the sniff test!
The three moons are naught but lies through and through. Only one moon has ever shone for us, and 'Kuutar' is her name.

dialogue.sit: The subjectivity is strong in this one...
We've heard something like this before in Natlan.

dialogue.t: The vast majority of ancient texts are filled with fanciful tales like these. I trust you understand my criteria a little better now.
Kuutar did not speak, merely gazing into the distance in silence. And where her gaze landed, this was her prophecy.
Clearly, whoever wrote this text never even met Kuutar — otherwise, they'd know that her eyes are always closed.
What about you, {NICKNAME}? What are you reading?

dialogue.sit: Seems like a collection of anecdotes.

dialogue.t: C'mon, let Paimon see...
The child wished to build a wooden nest with which to shield the fledgling bird from the cold. But being so young and lacking in strength, the child could not snap the branches from the trees...
Kuutar was passing by. Upon seeing the child, she summoned forth a kuuhenki, who built a beautiful nest for the child.
Ah, I remember that...
Not knowing the meaning of Kuutar's divine intervention, the child dared not to respond, and thus ran home to call their parents. But Kuutar was gone.

The Moonchanter declared the event a miracle and took the nest as a relic, placing it on high for all to see. The child was named as one favored by the goddess, and was greatly respected amongst the people...
Yet, no further miracles were bestowed, and this matter was forgotten in but a few years.
Huh. Any thoughts after reading that, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: If it's true...
It gives off a somewhat lonesome feeling.

dialogue.t: Yeah! Columbina probably just wanted to join the kid in making nests...
Ah... I had originally considered this a fabrication, because Kuutar did not perform any similar actions in subsequent records...
But now that I think about it, it does seem like something Columbina would do. It's just that...
She didn't know how other people would interpret her actions. She was probably worried about making things difficult for people... and so, she gradually stopped joining in...
Yes...
That's so sad.
*sigh*...
And now, I can make no such gestures of warmth even if I want to.
Let's see... There's Varka. Oh, and it's Durin and Albedo, too!

dialogue.sit: Talk about coincidences. We meet again.

dialogue.t: Yeah, this is pretty much the same place we bumped into each other last time.
Hahaha, I convinced them to stick around a little longer. We were all waiting on people, so I figured having a little company would help pass the time.
Ah, so you've been waiting for us? Does this mean that you've already arranged things with the Fatui?
Sure does. Now you're back, we can go meet up with them together. How'd your investigation at the Frostmoon Enclave go?
Well, we didn't find out Columbina's true name... but apart from that, it went pretty well.

dialogue.sit: We learned some stories from her early days.

dialogue.t: Aha, just as well that I didn't tag along, then. I'm sure our Moon Goddess wouldn't want every man and his dog knowing all about her private life... Still, desperate times, desperate measures, I guess. Someone had to do it.
So, Varka was waiting on us — but what about you two? Are you waiting for Alice?
Oh, no. We already met with her.
We discussed that experiment I mentioned to you last time. Oh, and she also handed me this communication device.

dialogue.sit: This looks familiar.
I'm sure I saw one of these back on the Golden Apple Archipelago...

dialogue.t: That's right. I understand she informed you about the relationship between the phantom phenomena and Teyvat's borders, yes? She wants me to help her with some more experiments on that front.
She said that she'll contact me through this device with more information.
Ah, I see. Following instructions and making observations — pretty common research method. Takes me right back to Albedo's lab...
Wait, then who exactly are you meeting?
Someone you know. Albedo's met him, too. But I don't think Miss Lauma or the Grand Master have been introduced...
Introductions are overrated — especially in cases like this.
It's you!
