So? It's not like the Akademiya has prohibitions against going abroad. Also, I applied for leave.
I've been writing to Hat Guy since obtaining a human form. I've already brought him up to speed on everything that's been going on in Nod-Krai.
Hat Guy...
Hat Guy...
Hmph...
Turns out I actually have heard that name before.
Oh... Then, why did you react the same way I did?
Haha, I only knew the name, not the fella! But since we're all here, let's do some introductions for what it's worth. I'm Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.
Lauma, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions.
And I'm a Driyosh from the Vahumana Darshan of the Sumeru Akademiya... Hat Guy.
Good to see you again, Mr. Guy. I believe we last saw each other on the boat ride here.

dialogue.sit: (So they came to Nod-Krai together...)

dialogue.t: Mmm. Mind you, the only reason I came here is because there's someone I want to look into.
Who's that?
The Doctor, also known as Dottore. Second of the Fatui Harbingers.

dialogue.sit: (Just as I thought...)

dialogue.t: From the tone of your voice... it sounds like there is bad blood between you.
...I was reviewing our archives and noticed that a lot of information about him was missing. Left a bad taste in my mouth. That's all there is to it.
Dottore... or Zandik as he was then known, once studied at the Akademiya. But he got kicked out before he could graduate.
Hahahaha! So the harbingers' number two man is a college dropout? How embarrassing for them.
Last we heard, he was planning something... We actually heard that a few times before even coming to Nod-Krai. But we haven't seen a trace of him since we got here.
He only appears when something interests him. For all we know, he might have left already.
But the fact that he did something here at all is worth noting... It'll fill a couple extra lines in his file.
Heh, why does it sound less like a file you're writing, and more like a criminal record...
Anyway, we were just about to meet two of the other Harbingers. Wanna come along? You might learn a thing or two about him there.
Sure.
Even though they're Harbingers, uh... Well, they're old acquaintances of ours, so... y'know, when you talk to them, try to be...
Hmph. I got it.
The Frostmoon Scions' relations with the Fatui remain tense. Forgive me if I do not attend.
In that case, we'll continue assisting Ms. Alice with her experiments.
Good stuff, everyone's having a fruitful time! Alright, we'd better get going — I'll lead the way.

dialogue.sit: Hey, {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}.

dialogue.t: Hmm?

dialogue.sit: Are you here for revenge?

dialogue.t: Well yeah, that's obviously part of it. But I'm not the only one who has a score to settle with him.
Neither you, nor Lesser Lord Kusanali, nor I want to see him meddling with things again.

dialogue.sit: Fair enough. One other thing...
When we return, let's talk about Columbina.

dialogue.t: Hah. What's the hurry?
Don't worry. Pigeons always know which way home is.

dialogue.sit: (Zandik? I've heard that name before... Back in the ruins, when the Ibis King mentioned that student — that was The Doctor?)

dialogue.t: You made it... Who is this?
A scholar from Sumeru. They call him Hat Guy. He's an old friend of {NICKNAME}.
Wait, THIS is the Akademiya representative you wrote about? He doesn't exactly look the part...
I believe this will prove my identity. You'll notice it bears the seal of the Sanctuary of Surasthana.
Well, what do you know. So it does... Alright then. My mistake.
It's fine. I expected as much.
What?
Ahem! So, as I mentioned in my letter, the Akademiya's got its eyes on Dottore.
But this matter remains top secret. Apart from those assisting in the investigation, the fewer people who know, the better.
If anyone asks, I am here in Nod-Krai to pursue my personal academic interests.
Gotta say, Varka, you did pretty well to keep all this under wraps for so long. Sounds like you got in touch with the Akademiya about this way back.
Haha, you flatter me.

dialogue.sit: You're all harbingers...
What reason would you have to disclose information about Dottore?

dialogue.t: Where do I even start? Hmph, remember that time we fought Rerir at Starsand Shoal? He sure let me have it then, didn't he? I'll bet Dottore had that all sketched out, with me as his convenient little pawn.
He could not care less about us if he tried. But hey, the feeling's mutual.
Does Dottore really strike you as the sort who values his relationships with his colleagues?
Fair point. Definitely not.
Which is why I always keep my guard up whenever he starts making suspicious moves. To that extent, our motivations align — on top of which, I consider you trustworthy people.

Now, back on topic. In the wake of the Rächer of Solnari episode, Sandrone and I grew suspicious about Dottore's complete inaction during the entire affair. So we tried to find out what he'd been up to — but unfortunately, to no avail.
He never lets anyone in on his plans. The more he cares about something, the more secretive he gets.
Indeed. Perhaps he believes that by keeping a low profile, he can avoid trouble. But that trick isn't going to work on his colleagues.
Yeah, I mean... He's been researching the Ancient Moon's Remnants, and he's been trying to get his paws on the Moon Marrows... Only an idiot would believe he doesn't have something more planned.
With this in mind, I returned to Snezhnaya and relayed my thoughts to Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, entreating her to have him recalled.
That's pretty direct. Did the Tsaritsa agree?
Yes. I made it abundantly clear that the Fatui's business in Nod-Krai is almost concluded, and we do not need three Harbingers in this territory. Her Majesty concurred.
Accordingly, Dottore has returned at her orders. I imagine he is continuing with experiments which no one besides he would ever have any interest in.
Common sense might mean nothing to him, but he's not stupid. He knows that no good can come from opposing the Tsaritsa.
Smarts alone won't get him all the way. He needs The Rooster's resources and Regrator's Mora — both of which the Tsaritsa can strip from him by waggling a finger.
But doesn't he have a track record of publicly following orders while going against them in private? He probably has it down to a fine art by now.
Wouldn't put it past him... We worked together on a research project once. Only briefly, but it was enough to show me that we're fundamentally different people.
He has no interest in doing things methodically, stage by stage. His thoughts jump all over the place, and the moment his curiosity is satisfied or he gets the results he wants, he disappears...
The only similarity we share is that, once we set our minds on doing something, we will see it done, whatever it takes.
We definitely saw some of that in your battle with Rerir. You got so competitive...
Ugh, do NOT remind me!
Then I believe we all concur: Dottore will not simply give up.
Tch. Fantastic, now this is turning into a whole day of unpleasant memories. Ugh!
Are you talking about the Moon Marrow stuff?
He also strikes me as the kind of person to disregard experimental regulations, ruin all the equipment, and go way over budget... then leave the first person he can find to deal with the fallout.

Exactly! This one time, he was running some high-temperature experiment and the substance exploded. But does he care? No! He orders his subordinates to open the device so he can observe the results — which causes the gas inside to leak out...
That gas was poisonous! If I hadn't been there, who knows how many people might've died?
And after all that? He left, while I was still cleaning up after his mess. "What a waste of time," he said.
Waste of time!? The nerve! HE wasted MY time!
Haha, you've been bottling that up for a while, huh?
Hat Guy, I must say — you seem awfully familiar with internal Fatui affairs... especially when it comes to Dottore.
Thank you, Lady Harbingers, for providing such valuable information. I have no other questions for now, so I'll be on my way.
Wait, what? You're just gonna leave!?
You're welcome to join if you want.
Ugh. Just when Paimon thought he'd finally mellowed out...
He makes quite the impression.
I'll say. I've met tons of headstrong people, but not many of them would join me in badmouthing Dottore...
Anyway, back to the main agenda. Varka, you said that Columbina has gone missing? Or rather, "disappeared"?
Yeah. We're working on building a connection between her and this world. The simplest method is to find out her real name.
I've actually asked her that question before, but she said she didn't know. Considering our relationship, I doubt she was lying to me.
(We'd only just met. Even if I knew, I wouldn't have told you...)

dialogue.sit: She could have just given you a pseudonym...
What did she do while she was with the Fatui?

dialogue.t: As far as I recall, she was never dispatched by Her Majesty to claim a Gnosis or anything like that.
The Tsaritsa's plans had long contained a place specifically for her.
I always thought that was weird. What could she do that the rest of us couldn't?
Knowing what we do now, it's probably something related to kuuvahki, right?
More than likely. When she first arrived, Columbina would often go to Her Majesty and ask when she could start the task assigned to her.
But Her Majesty always gave the same reply: "The time has not yet come." So she spent her days in Snezhnaya doing basically nothing.
"The Tsaritsa has summoned a beautiful blind maiden to be a Harbinger, giving her the third seat by virtue only of her enchanting voice."
It was a dumb and stupid rumor. But the reality of the situation made it hard to refute.
And what happened after that?
I imagine she stopped caring.
She no longer seemed to care why she had been recruited, and Her Majesty never gave her any missions, so she just... continued to sing in the flower garden.
For my part, I was busy — so busy, in fact, that watching someone be that idle had me fuming. But still, I got the sense that...
...That she had long been used to a life of other people claiming she was needed when she wasn't.
(I... just felt that having a place to stay would cost me something eventually.)
(And so I waited quietly for the day that I would have to pay the price...)
*sigh* And on the other end of that spectrum, you had me. Someone once told me that I had "the lousiest work and the toughest luck." Heh, that's a good way of putting it.
I forget who said it... But those words have always stuck with me.

dialogue.sit: (Sounds like something {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]} would say... No wonder.)

dialogue.t: (But you've done your job exceptionally well all this time. Because at heart, you are a conscientious person.)

dialogue.sit: Thanks for telling us all this.

dialogue.t: What is it? Something come to mind?

dialogue.sit: It's nothing. I'm just even more eager to learn her name now...
I want to shout it to her from the rooftops.

dialogue.t: Hehe, that makes sense. Nothing screams "you are needed!" like your name shouted from across the town.
Well, good luck with it. But if you ask me, "Columbina" is still the most shoutable name.
I'm just so used to it now, after all the arguments we've had. I can't be bothered trying to remember another name for her.
Nor I.
(Sandrone... Arlecchino...)

dialogue.sit: You chat further about interesting moments from Columbina's past. But soon, the time comes for you to part.

dialogue.t: Huh, it's a Seelie! Does that mean Nicole has news for us?
Ladies, I thank you for your hospitality. If the chance ever comes up, I definitely owe you both a drink sometime.
I'm sure it will.
You can make your own way out. Heck, you've been here enough times, you probably know your way around better than I do.

dialogue.sit: Take care, everyone.
We'll be in touch if the situation changes.

dialogue.t: Okay, time to do what adventurers do best — follow that Seelie!
Here you are.
Ah, Hat Guy.
How come you're back so soon? Did things go alright with the Fatui?
Fine. Dottore's been summoned home by the Tsaritsa. Couldn't get much more than that.
How about you? Any progress with the investigation?
Unfortunately not...
We've tried everything. Different phantoms, different locations, different points in history, but the results are the same each time.
Abyssal monsters roaming the land, people crying out in despair, with no hope of being rescued.
Every time I see it, I can't help but think... is this what it was like in Mondstadt when Dragonspine-Durin attacked?
And... if I fail in the task I've been given... will I create yet another tragedy?
...That's just meaningless speculation.
When we encountered similar phenomena previously, I tried to interfere with those illusions, using sounds and lights to guide them.
However, we could not change their fates. At most, we were able to extend their existences.
The events of the past are like fate that has been written into Irminsul. There isn't a living thing in Teyvat that can escape its past...
But Ms. Alice instructed us to try to find ways to change the outcome that these phantoms face.
It's an impossible task. Can't you just refuse?
Since she asked us to do this, I feel like it can't truly be impossible. Or, if it is... Well, mages can make the impossible possible.
I could not have been born as "Durin" otherwise.
But you also said that your past thirty-nine attempts were fruitless.
That's true...
But you're still going?
Yes.
After this many futile attempts, surely you realize that you're not doing this because you still believe what some mage told you.
It's because you want her hypothesis to come true. It's something you wish for deep inside.
So, think for yourself about what you want to do. As long as you don't believe it's futile, it isn't.
...Yeah!
Previous experience indicates that we cannot touch the phantoms, which limits the effectiveness of our interventions.
If we want to clear this hurdle, we need to break this rule somehow.
Same thought here. Following the same rules means repeating the same failures — reducing ourselves to mere playthings of fate.
So you mean... we need to figure out a way to make contact with them, despite knowing that we can't?
Yes. And I suspect that's something only you are capable of.
Everything in Teyvat is logged in Irminsul, but The Withering that once occurred in Sumeru was a sign that that great world tree was being corrupted.
This corruption allowed things that should not have existed in Teyvat to appear... This is tantamount to rewriting reality to an extent.
You're saying, Abyssal power might be able to affect these phantoms?
No one's ever tried it before. If you're gonna try it, it'll take courage, and you have to be confident that you can control it.
Is anyone there!? Has anyone seen my daughter...?
She's missing. I... I have to find her...
I hear someone inside... Spargana? Are you in there?
Aaaargh!
If I can use my Abyssal powers to warn him that there is danger here... maybe it'll change his decision. Maybe he'll stay away.
Yes. The important thing is not the nature of the power, but rather how you use it.
To intimidate and obstruct... Hmph. Sounds about right for the Abyss.
...Let me try. I should be able to influence that thing.
He... He really left! We did it!
Don't celebrate too soon. Follow him, see what he does next.
The barrier's gone too. How odd...
Anyway, I guess I'll keep going.
Quickly, let's keep up.
So many... monsters...!
There's still a chance, Durin. Use the traps.
This is a new development... I've never seen this happen before...
We might just be able to save this person.
Hello there... Have you seen my daughter? Spargana's her name. She's carrying a large backpack...
...Get out while you still can, you fool... You won't find any survivors here...
But I can't just leave her here. She must be so scared right now...
*sigh* ...Sorry, wish I could help, but I haven't seen her. You'll just have to keep looking.
Okay. Thank you.
If I do find her, I'll get her to shelter and come back for you.
Don't bother. I've got nowhere left to go.
What's that noise...?
M—Monster... Aaaaahhh!
...If he goes inside, he'll be walking into a trap. Let's try this once more — this time, we have to stop him.
Hello there. I'm looking for my daughter. She carries a large backpack. Have you seen her?
I did see a few young girls... None with a backpack, but surely she would've ditched it, no?
*sigh* What are you even doing here? How are you going to get back out?
Not only are there monsters, but there's explosives too... If only my legs would work properly, I'd... *cough*
That's fine. That's all I needed to hear. Thanks for telling me.
Ugh, another monster...
Aaaaaaggghhh!
I guess we can't let him in here either.
H—Hello, I'm looking for... Huh!?
Looking for what? Everything here belongs to me!
Get him, boys!
Aghhh!
Huh? That's... That looks like one of my daughter's books!
Oh, thank you, thank you...
Yes, it's one of hers for sure — there's her name on it, right there! She left her backpack here.
Durin, just like last time! Use the explosives!
It won't work... there's not enough left. If he makes it in, he'll die.
But then... This clue could be the key to him finding his daughter...
It might not be the only one. Better he misses that clue than loses his life.
I guess so...
That's my daughter's book! She's passed this way! Why... Why won't you let me go in!?
I've searched, and searched, and searched... just for this! But how will I find her without any clues!?
I no longer have anywhere else to go...
I'm sorry... I'm so sorry...
He refuses to go anywhere else... Whether he opens this door or not, all that awaits him now is death. We... couldn't change his fate.
Albedo, Hat Guy, let's try one more time. I don't know how we're going to do this, but I don't want to give up either.
Why am I here... What's going on? All these scenes running through my head... Where are they from?
Huh? What's going on?
His reactions have changed.
How many times have I... What's happening to me? I—I...
Huh. Wait. Who are you?
Y—You can see us now?
I... feel like I always could, but that I only just "realized" you were there... I'm sorry. I don't know how to describe what I'm feeling.
But... You were the ones guiding me using that marked barrier, right?
I haven't done anything yet, but those monsters, those deaths... They feel like memories. Like things I really did experience...
I... I won't find my daughter. In fact, I'll ultimately die trying to find her. Isn't that right?
Wh... No, it isn't.
Yes, it is.
Even so, we're trying to find a way out of this.
You've not seen my daughter either, have you?
Hmm...
It seems she really isn't here...
Ugh... Oh... Ohh...
...I'm sorry we couldn't help you.
I'm just... tired. Maybe this is destiny. Maybe it doesn't matter how hard I search...
How long do I have left?
Experience says fifteen to twenty minutes.
Fifteen to twenty... *sigh*
Thank you for all your help. Let's rest a while. You look exhausted too...
Now's not the time for you to start pitying us.
Haha, it's not pity... I'm just... realizing that I've only got ten or so minutes left, you know?
You say you're from Mondstadt, yes? A place with windmills, where the people enjoy limitless freedom?
And you're from Sumeru, where they've built an academy into a giant tree?
Yes. It seems you've never heard of either place.
Those names are unknown to me, I'm afraid, yes. Have you heard of Hyperborea?
I have, but... I heard that it was destroyed in the distant past...
I see. That was where my ancestors once lived. What about Delphi Pytho? Was it later rebuilt?
I've never heard that name.
Then what about Sal Vindagnyr?
I have seen that name on stone tablets on Dragonspine, but I'm afraid the only things left of that place are its ruins.
I see... Sure enough, there was no way to turn this around, huh...
*sigh* I'm sorry. I was the one who asked to chat, but it seems like we're too many ages apart. There's barely any common ground to start from.
It's alright. We did hear something new, at least.
From how you speak of your lives, things must be going alright for you, I guess?
They are. Mondstadt is a place of freedom and happiness. There's a lot of good people in the Church and the Knights of Favonius, and even outsiders find that it's an easy place to feel at home.
We have festivals a few times a year... everyone gets together to drink, sing, and be merry...
Sumeru's a lot more uptight. Not really the kind of place where you can relax. It's a nation fraught with problems wherever you look.
But if all you want in life is to seek knowledge, I guess it's pretty much paradise.
That's wonderful.
In other words, after this all-devouring black tide passed, humanity did not merely avoid extinction, but rose to build prosperous civilizations anew.
I mean, I can see you all right now. That must mean the future isn't a total mess, right?
...That's true.
Well, time's almost up. Let's part ways, I think. Might be best if you don't waste too much time on me.
The chances are slim, I know, but I'd like to spend these last few minutes looking for Spargana. If things work out, I'd love to tell her about all that I've heard.
May we meet again... Well, or not, most probably... In that case, may your wishes come true.
He's gone. In a few minutes, he will meet the end that was his to begin with.
The ending of this tale did not change, but I believe that we've just made the most progress we have yet.
"May your wishes come true"... If only it were so simple.
Hat Guy, could I ask you a question?
Hmm?
You've never talked about your past. It seems complicated... and it weighs heavily on you, too.
Would you be willing to tell me about it? I mean, sometimes it's better to get things out in the open. Take that guy we tried to help, for instance — at least he said goodbye with a smile, right?
I know about Albedo's past. Our experiences are very similar, and he created me.
As for you, you're my first friend, and you've witnessed every step I've taken. But by comparison, I know nothing about you.
Either way, I mean, we're still best friends! But... if I knew more about you, I might understand your thoughts a bit better...
I've told you about myself. I'm a student at the Akademiya.
And what did you do before that?
Prepared for the entrance exam.
...Alright. If you really don't want to talk about it, I won't press you any further.
I was a puppet bu{RUBY#[D]Simulanka}ilt from the branches of a white tree, using technology left behind by the Khaenri'ahn schools of mechanical engineering.
A white tree? You mean an Irminsul tree?
Yes. A branch of Irminsul that was once connected to the main tree.
So you had a human creator too...
Yeah. But my creator abandoned me after deciding that I was a failure.
After that...
Durin, resisting the influence of the Abyss, suppressing the urge to destroy, trying to do the right thing... None of these things are easy.
But no matter how hard they are, trying to rewrite past wrongs is far harder.
You asked me if you would create a new tragedy if you failed. I told you there was no point speculating about that.
But the real answer is... Yes. You absolutely will.
Hat Guy...
But at least you've got people here to help steer you away from the wrong path. So... just keep aiming towards the light.
I will. I promise.
Alright. Break time's over.
Dodo!
Hello? Durin speaking...
Hello friends, it's me. What have you been up to, hmm? I'm detecting some unmistakable fluctuations here at the border.
The amplitude isn't particularly high, but they're completely different signals from the ones before. And the scale is comparable to those I've detected previously.
Alice, we were unable to save that person. However, he appears to have retained a portion of the memories gained through that cycle, and was able to hold a conversation with us.
I see... Well, that is rather odd indeed. It definitely merits further attention.
Could I trouble you to keep trying the same approach? I need to gather some more data. Counting on you~!
...Hmm, I should probably have Nicole come and check this out as well.
There you are. I was worried you might stop to collect treasure chests opened by the Seelie along the way... It would have taken you so much longer to get here.
(*sigh*... Another conversation I cannot hear...)
I am delighted to see that you understand what takes priority, and that your adventurer's instinct has not swayed your resolve. Really, I must applaud you for it... You should know—
(Agh, Paimon's head...)
...Okay, I'll try and keep it short... My senses are telling me that this is where we shall find the entrance to the ruins.
Oh, cool. Well, what are we waiting for? Let's open it up and see!
Patience. This was a sanctuary of great importance to the Hyperboreans. A special process is required to open the gate.
Oh... like the place that housed the Eternal Moon's Marrow?

dialogue.sit: Seems like the ancients were very fond of making tricky gate puzzles...

dialogue.t: Mkay, so what's the plan? Need us to do anything? ...Uh, and just the short version, if you can!
Ah. Alright then. I was planning to start with some background on the invention of these techniques... Are you sure you don't want to hear it? It's quite informative.
Remember what you were saying about priorities...?
Fine. Simply put, we need three human representatives to successfully undergo a process of kuuvahki resonance.
Think of it as a test from the three moon goddesses to see if the entrants are qualified, with the most recognizable qualification being kuuvahki.
Pretty sure Lauma would ace that test! ...Oh, wait, but we need three people...
I also have no doubt that the Moonchanter would be qualified. But we would need two other people with the same constitution.
Therefore, the most feasible method is not so much to follow the rules, but to figure out how the test functions and find a workaround.
I've done some research, and it turns out the mechanism is rather crude. We'll simply need humans to stand before it who have sufficient kuuvahki energy within them.
I'm with you so far. How do we get the kuuvahki in them?
Hmm... The easiest way would be transfusion. Take some kuuvahki from Nod-Krai's soil, put it into the bloodstream, and get it circulating in the body.
So, we're going to... cheat on the test?
Precisely. There are other methods, but this is the simplest one. Cheating the system is much easier than trying to hide from it.
Sorry? Does the idea of cheating upset you, Miss Lauma?
...No, that's not it. I just... I suddenly had an idea!
Ooh, what is it?
It's about Moon-Prayer Night. I've figured out a way for Kuutar to join in the festivities!
But as Paimon said, we need to have our priorities straight. Let's get back to the test — I'll follow up with Nefer on the festival arrangements.
Oh, uh, okay. Anyway, is this really the best method we have? A kuuvahki transfusion sounds dangerous, no matter how you slice it...
If you think that's dangerous, wait till you hear the other methods... I'd be more than happy to go through them if you'd like? There are several—
No need! We're good! Let's go with this one!
Very well. Kuuvahki transfusion it is. Now, I should mention that the risks can be greater or lower depending on individual compatibility.
It would be rash to simply infuse the kuuvahki and hope for the best. If the body rejects it, the reaction can be quite severe.
The symptoms are similar to another condition that some people living here suffer from, known as congenital kuuvahki sensitivity.
So, before we execute our plan, I will perform a simple test of my own to see who is compatible, and who is not.

Once that is done, we will have to complete the resonance process as rapidly as possible. The participants must remain stationary while the kuuvahki circulates and bonds with them, and they mustn't eat or drink anything.
What? No eating or drinking?
That's some hardcore fasting... They'll all be monks by the time they're through.

dialogue.sit: How long will they have to keep that up?

dialogue.t: Three days.
That's so long! And we still need to find two more people who are not just compatible, but also willing to volunteer...
(Fasting...? What are they talking about...?)

dialogue.sit: I'm willing to volunteer.

dialogue.t: Really? Don't you wanna think this through?
Haha, count me in, too. Three days without food? I can handle that.
Ms. Nicole has made it clear that this is the easiest way. The way I see it, there's nothing else to discuss. It's time to step up.

dialogue.sit: Compared to having Columbina disappear completely...
...Fasting for a few days is nothing.

dialogue.t: Yeah. You're right. I—In that case, Paimon volunteers to be captain of logistics! She'll keep the fires lit and grab some spare clothes to keep you comfortable!

dialogue.sit: Good work, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Then we'll start with you first, {NICKNAME}. Please step forward.
How is it going? Do you feel anything?

dialogue.sit: No.

dialogue.t: How about now?

dialogue.sit: No.

dialogue.t: And now?

dialogue.sit: Still nothing.

dialogue.t: Huh... Wh—What about now?

dialogue.sit: Nothing at all.
Did you do something?

dialogue.t: You guys... it's not a competition, you know...
Alright, I'm officially impressed. Even as a Descender, you can withstand far more than I imagined...
It's like I summoned a giant stone titan to arm wrestle you, and your arm hasn't even moved an inch.
In my last attempt, I infused five times the amount of kuuvahki required.

dialogue.sit: That much!?

dialogue.t: Yes. Safe to say, compatibility won't be an issue for you. You're eligible to join.
You're next, Mr. Varka.
Sure. Here goes nothing.
Alright. I'll start where we left off — five times the required kuuvahki dose...
Whoa whoa whoa, hey, hey, wait a minute...
Ugh... Ugh...
Uh... How's it going?
N—Not great, I uh... kinda wanna puke. Feels like I've been drinking too much... a few bottles of wine, then a big stein of "Dark Horse"... with some hard liquor from Liyue mixed in...
Hehe.
You think this is funny? I just lost to a young lady in an arm-wrestling contest. I'm never gonna live that down!
My apologies. I'll lower the concentration and try again.
How's it going now?
I'm not as dizzy as last time, but I can still feel it pulsing around.
In that case, you wouldn't be an ideal choice, Mr. Varka. Let's try someone else.
Okay, let's go ask some of our other friends, then!
No surprises here, Miss Moonchanter. You're perfectly compatible. You may join.
I'm getting a slight headache.
Shame. You were so close.
Whoa, I—I'm itching all over...
Allergic reaction. We can't have that.
Well? Are you gonna start or what?
The Hexenzirkel is an organization that cares for and protects children. We will not have them do dangerous things — not even tests.
Is something the matter?
The candidates have to be human.
(I guess that rules me out too.)
Huh, everyone except the Moonchanter got beaten. Guess I don't need to feel so bad after all... Ahem, uh, I mean, looks like this isn't gonna be as easy as we thought.
Perhaps I could ask for volunteers among the Frostmoon Scions.
Hmm... I'll see about talking to some trusted Lightkeeper colleagues. Illuga springs to mind.
In fact, I think we had some former Frostmoon Scions join our ranks recently.
Can you gimme the scientific explanation for how the test works? I can probably make some kind of test-bot.
Then, we can just zip through Nasha Town, going up to people and pressing a button to check their status. Wouldn't that be way easier?
No.
Wow, no elaboration for once!
How about I contact the Knights of Favonius garrison in the Wavechaser Plain? Shame that Lohen's already left. That guy's even tougher than I am...
Strange... The moon goddess is clearly revered by many people, so why is she on the brink of disappearing?
She mentioned that the world has rejected her from the very beginning...
And when we fought the Rächer of Solnari, it seemed like she exhausted her power for our sake...
Also, Paimon's not sure "revered" is the right word for how people feel about her.
Gratitude, certainly. For my part, anyway.
It's basic reciprocity. She helped us, so she deserves our help in return.
Yeah, even though she looked like she didn't care... She still saved a ton of people — including me.
A review of the relevant data leads me to conclude that Miss Columbina is a good person.
Yup, you bet!
(They really think so...?)
I'm super surprised that "Columbina" isn't her actual name, though. I think it really suits her. It's light and graceful, and... yeah, just a really pretty name!
I know, right?
Unfortunately, that's not our decision to make.
("Columbina"... That was the codename the Fatui gave me. But it also came up in the song I heard when I was born...)
(But... is that really all there is to it? What do I truly think of my own name...?)
(Is there anyone left who will still call me by that name?)

dialogue.sit: (...She told me to pick whichever name took my fancy. Why did I pick "Columbina"?)
(Maybe because I felt that she never wanted to become Kuu{RUBY#[S]The Moon Maiden}tar, and be worshiped as a god...)

dialogue.t: Moon-Prayer Night is getting closer by the day. We're running out of time. We need to look for other candidates.
Then allow me to try.
Huh? What are you doing here?
You contacted your friends via the Adventurers' Guild. Sandrone has been keeping an eye out for something like that, so she informed me.
Since I have the ability to accommodate a Moon Marrow, I should prove to be a suitable candidate.
(Arlecchino...)
When can we begin?
I see... We can begin right away.
How was it? Did you feel any discomfort?
None at all.
Then it seems we shan't need to look for additional candidates after all.
Great!
Cool. Alright, like Paimon said, the rest of us can take turns making sure the three of 'em stay warm and comfy.
Then my job is to take care of the caretakers. I will ensure everyone receives food and accommodation.

dialogue.sit: Let's do this. No time to waste.

dialogue.t: I'm ready as well.
The work is done, the sacred scroll shut. The stars grow dim, the people silent. The white sun sets, the silver moon rises. O path to the temple, appear now before us.
Wow, it really opened!
(So that's what all this is about. They've been trying to open this gate...)
With a calm mind, this proved not too arduous. Come, let us enter.

dialogue.sit: Wait...

dialogue.t: It might be best to eat something first. Take care to chew properly and swallow slowly. It will give your body time to readjust to the digestion process.
(They will head in soon.)
(They will need to enter this gate...)
Huh...?
(I... cannot pass through. Is it because I have no physical body?)
Ugh... Aah...
(It has been three days... My strength has all but completely faded...)
(Can I really... hold on until Moon-Prayer Night...?)

quests.description: After reaching an understanding, you decide to head back to the Silvermoon Hall to ask around about what kind of gifts Columbina likes.
